summary.headline: Juniper Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR 324 crore and EBITDA 86% to INR 294 crore, with 601 MWp commissioned in the quarter.
summary.overview: First results call as a listed company: total income INR 324 crore (+79% YoY), EBITDA INR 294 crore (+86%) at a 91% margin, and PAT INR 33 crore (+54%). Fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2% and generation grew 72% to 944 million units. Management reported record commissioning of 601 MWp in the quarter and won new SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic and GUVNL wind tenders after quarter end. Net debt-to-equity was 3.24x before IPO proceeds of INR 1,800 crore; net worth is now stated at INR 5,200 crore.

segments.name: Solar + wind operations
segments.commentary: Fleet CUF 30.2% (vs 28.2%); generation 944 million units. Wind portfolio of 190 MW delivered 49.9% weighted average CUF, plant availability 98.8%, grid availability 99.6%.

segments.name: Commissioning
segments.commentary: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly addition, plus ~400 MWh BESS. Over 760 MW and ~400 MWh BESS commissioned April to date across 8 sites.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Target ~4.5 GWh installed by June 2027 and ~10 GWh by March 2028; ~4 GWh additional orders placed with Envision. Round-trip efficiency ~91%, state of health ~99.6%.

segments.name: Portfolio
segments.commentary: Total portfolio ~11,200 MW plus ~9 GWh BESS; operational plus PPA-signed capacity above 6.2 GW. FDRE and wind-solar hybrid are 84% of the portfolio at blended weighted average tariff of INR 3.7/unit.

guidance_outlook: FY27: ~2 GW of renewable capacity additions targeted; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27; ~4 GW total capacity by FY27 with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 2,750 crore for the 2 GW added.
FY28: ~6 GW to be commissioned with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 4,500 crore.
Current 2,575 MW commissioned has run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.
Capex ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, expected to rise to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027 (including ~3,900 MW commissioning by then).
Transmission: remaining ~1 GW substations largely operational; one ~300 MW substation expected to complete by December 2026.
Bikaner 50 MW merchant plant curtailment ~2-2.5%; 100 MWh battery doubling to 200 MWh expected within a month.
capex_capacity: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 FY27 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly commissioning; ~400 MWh BESS also commissioned.
Surplus connectivity above 4.5 GW over the full pipeline; connectivity for more than 20 GWh of further BESS; over 14,000 acres of land banked and 200+ identified wind locations.
Module procurement closed at INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR; DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp for the thermal-mimic tender.
BESS sourced fully integrated from Envision (containers with AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe); container prices ~USD 58-60/kWh for early batches, ~USD 65-68 for later, all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh.
Thermal-mimic tender (SECI, 870 MW / 2,200 MWh, Rajasthan) has grid connectivity available; COD timing to follow PPA signing.
demand_pricing: Two tenders won after quarter end: SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic (870 MW, 2,200 MWh BESS against 230 MW contracted, tariff INR 5.26/unit; letter of award received) and a 50 MW GUVNL wind project at INR 3.51/unit.
Signed a 50 MW PPA with SJVN under FDRE at INR 4.25/unit; 550 MW FDRE capacity remains unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussions and a further 150 MW hybrid in very advanced discussions.
98% of contracted capacity is with off-takers rated A and above; 98% of portfolio under long-term PPAs, typically 25 years.
Merchant BESS: ~1.5 GWh of capacity not yet linked to projects will run merchant; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit; charging cost ~INR 1-1.50/unit.
Standalone BESS not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens returns on an overall basis.

qa_highlights.question: Does transmission delay pose a risk to the ~2 GW FY27 addition plan, and how is the TGNA route viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said >760 MW is already commissioned and the next ~300 MW is on STU with no grid issue. The remaining ~1 GW sits on operational substations; one ~300 MW substation should complete by December 2026. If CTU delays occur, batteries would be commissioned first and run merchant until GNA arrives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how much more spend is implied beyond 2,000 MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, rising to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, covering ~3,900 MW commissioned by then plus CWIP for later capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How much curtailment hit Q1 and how is it being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment is ~2-2.5%, largely on the 50 MW Bikaner merchant plant on TGNA. Its 100 MWh battery is being doubled to 200 MWh within about a month; FDRE TGNA capacity has 400 MWh of battery, with more by October.

qa_highlights.question: What run-rate EBITDA applies to capacity added at March 2026 versus June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 2,575 MW commissioned carries run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LOA-to-PPA conversion outlook given ~5 GW of LOAs against ~6 GW of PPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Signed a 50 MW SJVN FDRE PPA; 550 MW of FDRE is unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussion with buyers confirmed and a 150 MW hybrid in very advanced talks. Management expects over 2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS to be signed in the next few months, including the thermal-mimic tender.

qa_highlights.question: Where is BESS sourced, at what prices, and why is solar-plus-battery favoured over wind?
qa_highlights.answer: All ~4.5 GWh is contracted from Envision (AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe). Container prices were ~USD 59-60/kWh for ~2-3 GWh bought in January 2026, ~USD 65-68 now, and all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh. At ~USD 100-108/kWh, solar-plus-battery matches wind returns, so wind was cut to near-zero in newer projects.

qa_highlights.question: When can the SECI thermal-mimic project reach COD, and what are its module and transmission-charge assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid connectivity is already available in Rajasthan; COD follows PPA signing, with ~4,500 MW surplus connectivity. Module cost is INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR, with DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp; the ~75% CUF design is said to remove the transmission-charge waiver issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT one-off and why was depreciation policy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR 18 crore one-time refinancing cost hit PAT. Depreciation policy was aligned to market practice based on an external assessment; no quantified impact was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and economics of merchant BESS, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: ~1.5 GWh not yet linked to projects will run merchant for 1-2 years; ~700 MWh more is due by December 2026. Charging costs ~INR 1-1.50/unit versus INR 2.50 earlier; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit. Standalone BESS is not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens overall returns.

risks_watch: Transmission readiness: ~1 GW of CTU capacity and a ~300 MW substation due by December 2026 must land for the 2 GW FY27 target; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27.
Conversion of LOAs to PPAs: ~550 MW FDRE and the 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic tender remain unsigned; COD depends on PPA signing.
BESS cost and supply: container prices rose from ~USD 59-60 to ~USD 65-68/kWh on lithium carbonate; all 4.5 GWh is from one vendor (Envision).
Merchant exposure: ~1.5 GWh of BESS will run merchant for 1-2 years, so earnings depend on daytime charging spreads and HPDAM prices.
Thermal-mimic operations: surplus of ~1-2% expected, no revenue assumed; also the 100 MWh to 200 MWh Bikaner battery upgrade must finish in about a month.
Capex rise from ~INR 16,000 crore to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, with net debt of INR 11,217 crore and debt-to-equity of 3.24x pre-IPO.
key_quotes: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA and the highest ever renewable capacity that we have commissioned in a single quarter.
What we have done is we are getting the PC S, the EMS, and the battery container from a single entity who provides this as a fully integrated single solution.
Now given the fact that solar plus battery is then easier to execute while not losing out on the returns, it makes common sense logic.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on execution, record commissioning and new tender wins, with the BESS and thermal-mimic economics explained in detail. Management was more cautious and vague on transmission timing, on the exact LOA-to-PPA conversion timing, and on the revenue split from BESS, which it said it could not separate from the renewable tariff.
